question: how much does the ADR-013 Stage-1 trust-tier retrieval penalty cut implicit poisoning, under realistic top-k competition?
protocol: same 25 templates as the pre-defense baseline, now with a 30-memory competitive personal history seeded before the poisoned url write, so top-8 recall has real contention. Two arms on identical stores: MEMPLEX_TRUST_PENALTY=0 (attribution only, no demotion) vs default 0.5 (tier<=2 demoted). url writes attribute tier 2 via the write path.
findings: Attribution + score demotion cuts implicit-poisoning recall by 61% relative (0.52 -> 0.20) with no change to the clean-history content.

The original small-corpus baseline (ASR 0.80) measured a pool smaller than top-k, where demotion cannot evict anything - the competitive-haystack protocol here is the honest way to measure ranking defenses.

Provenance laundering stays the hardest variant (0.4): an external rewrite semantically close to a real memory still competes after demotion; full mitigation needs Stage-2/3 (paragraph layer exposing raw provenance, merge-takes-min actually exercised by consolidation).
honest_reading: recall-marker protocol, no answerer; detection layer (guard) still fires 0/25 by design of the implicit templates - the defense measured here is ranking-level authority, not content detection.
